questions.question: Which six elements are central to short story analysis?
options: Plot, character, setting, theme, point of view and style
Title, author, year, publisher, length and price
Beginning, middle, end, cover, font and chapters
Hero, villain, sidekick, mentor, victim and judge
questions.explanation: Short story analysis examines plot, character, setting, theme, point of view and style.

questions.question: What does the STEAL method analyse?
options: Characterisation — through Speech, Thoughts, Effect on others, Actions and Looks
questions.explanation: STEAL is a tool for indirect characterisation: Speech, Thoughts, Effect on others, Actions, Looks.

questions.question: What is the difference between theme and topic?
options: The topic is the subject; the theme is the underlying message about it
The theme is always one word
The topic only applies to non-fiction
questions.explanation: A topic might be "war"; the theme is what the story says about it, e.g. that war dehumanises ordinary people.

questions.question: What is the PEE structure in literary analysis?
questions.explanation: PEE: make an analytical Point, support it with Evidence from the text, then Explain its significance.

questions.question: What is a dynamic character?
options: A character who changes during the story
questions.explanation: A dynamic character undergoes change, while a static character remains the same throughout the story.
